clue.text: Alan Clark-type sticking member in pop songstress?

indicators.note: sticking a member into something signals putting one piece inside another
in tells us where the member goes: inside the singer's name

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
an arm is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A seductive Tory politician is pictured inserting himself where he shouldn't, in true Private Eye fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Clark was a Tory minister famed for his diaries and his success with women. 'sticking' hints at sex, but with 'in' it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark was a notorious womaniser and smooth seducer, the type of man called a charmer.

clue.text: See 9
Not-so-famous 'Gazza' loses his head and sees the light!

indicators.note: his head is his first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: Bamber Gascoigne, the University Challenge quizmaster, a less famous Gascoigne than footballer Paul, called Gazza

explanation.surface: An unknown footballer losing his head and having a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: Gazza was footballer Paul Gascoigne; the other Gascoigne is TV quiz host Bamber. 'loses his head' drops the first letter of BAMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the middle traffic signal, between red and green.

clue.text: Live comics about to go off ruthless leader

indicators.note: go off means take off, and the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Comedians on stage turning against a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go off' says C (about) goes off LIVE COMICS, and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobodan Milosevic was the Serbian president accused of war crimes in the Balkan wars.

clue.text: Where to land, around one, Lord Lucan, for instance

indicators.note: the landing strip goes around the letter for one

parts.note: planes land on a runway
A means one

explanation.surface: Where the vanished Lord Lucan might have touched down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts the runway about A. Lord Lucan vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered, and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucan fled and disappeared, so he is an example of a fugitive.

clue.text: Left is in worse surroundings — peer takes the piss out of this

definitions.text: peer takes the piss out of this

indicators.note: the worse word forms surroundings around the letter for left

parts.note: badder is a jokey colloquial comparative of bad, meaning worse

explanation.surface: A nobleman mocking someone in a worse place than him, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' puts BADDER around L. 'peer' is not a nobleman but someone who pees, and 'takes the piss out of' is meant literally, not as mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: The urine stored in the body's bladder is what anyone peeing empties out of it.

clue.text: Hairstyle busy creatures feel at home with?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall, rounded bouffant hairdo

definitions.text: busy creatures feel at home with?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: bees, busy creatures, live in a hive

explanation.walkthrough: 'busy creatures' are bees; the question mark flags the playful second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the high piled 1960s hairdo and the home of bees.

clue.text: Incense: hazard when going topless

indicators.note: losing the top, the first letter, in a down entry

parts.note: a danger is a hazard

explanation.surface: The risks of perfumed smoke when sunbathing bare-chested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the first letter of DANGER. 'Incense' looks like perfumed smoke, but it is the verb, to make angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense is to enrage, so it can mean to anger someone.

clue.text: Scarper when party errand boy grabs one

indicators.note: the pieces grab the letter, holding it between them

parts.note: a do is a party
a runner carries messages and runs errands
A means one

explanation.surface: An errand boy makes off with something from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabs' has the two pieces hold A between them. Scarper is British slang for run away; to do a runner is to flee, often without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for making a hasty escape.

clue.text: Would-be re-emergent novelist's career to bite the dust?

parts.note: to career is to rush along
to bite the dust is to die

explanation.surface: A writer's comeback career looks doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb, to hurtle. Salman Rushdie lived in hiding under a death fatwa and was trying to re-emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Satanic Verses hid for years under the fatwa and wanted to return to public life.

clue.text: Opportunist lawyer offers conveyance for injured parties plus trailer

parts.note: an ambulance carries the injured to hospital
a chaser trails after something, following it

explanation.surface: A shady lawyer is offering a hospital vehicle and a trailer, like a dodgy car dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 1 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance chaser is a lawyer who seeks out accident victims to drum up compensation claims for profit.

clue.text: Clearly over the pretty little head of many an ambitious female?

definitions.text: Clearly over the pretty little head of many an ambitious female?

parts.words: Clearly over the pretty little head of many an ambitious female?
parts.note: something transparent (clearly) placed above the head of women seeking promotion: the invisible barrier to their advancement

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 19 Down. 'Clearly' hints at the glass, 'over the head' at the ceiling, while the patronising phrase 'pretty little head' mocks sexist attitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the unseen barrier that stops women rising to senior positions at work.

clue.text: Aristocrats' organs without number

definitions.note: the possessive stands in for the plural noun; the 's reads as is

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the organs go around the number

parts.note: ears are organs of hearing
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Body parts of noblemen, lacking a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside, so EARS wraps around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are members of the British peerage, ranking just below a marquess.

clue.text: Flog song collection

parts.note: to flog someone is to whip them
a round is a song for voices entering one after another

explanation.surface: Selling off a collection of songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' reads as sell, British slang, but here it is to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal collection of money among a group, such as colleagues buying a leaving present.

clue.text: Put-upon employee makes it one against five in Murdoch's outfit

indicators.note: in places the three letters inside the broadcaster's name

parts.note: Sky was the satellite broadcaster controlled by Rupert Murdoch
I is the Roman numeral one
v is short for versus, against
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A worker at a Murdoch company complains of being outnumbered five to one.
explanation.walkthrough: Murdoch's News Corporation ran the satellite TV company Sky; 'in' puts IVV inside it. A skivvy is a British term for a lowly domestic servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A skivvy does the menial drudgery for others, so is an exploited, put-upon worker.

clue.text: Many interesting positions in here should Mrs. T. get involved with AA(UK) on one

indicators.note: letters getting involved with each other are mixed together and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Mrs T, the nickname for Margaret Thatcher
the letters as written, the UK Automobile Association
A means one

explanation.surface: Imagining Margaret Thatcher mixing with the Automobile Association.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs T was Margaret Thatcher. 'get involved with' shuffles MRST, AAUK and A together.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Indian book on love is famous for describing a great variety of sexual postures.

clue.text: Government enterprise stifles political understanding

indicators.note: the phrase smothers the answer, holding it within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of government and the start of enterprise

explanation.surface: State-run businesses smothering political agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifles' tells you the phrase holds the answer: it sits in 'governmENT ENTErprise'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale of Britain and France.

clue.text: Dithering oily brat, Brown finally makes leader

indicators.note: dithering suggests wavering back and forth, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of Brown

parts.note: N is the final letter of Brown

explanation.surface: An indecisive smarmy child, with Gordon Brown at his side, becomes Labour leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives N from Brown; 'Dithering' shuffles it with OILY BRAT, a jab at Blair's ally Gordon Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair led the Labour Party from 1994 and became prime minister in 1997.

clue.text: Mike briefly into cola distribution gets rich

indicators.note: distribution spreads the letters around into a new order

parts.note: mic is the short form of microphone, often spelt mike

explanation.surface: A man called Mike gets rich in the soft-drinks business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich' looks like wealthy, but means laughable, as in 'that's rich!'. 'distribution' shuffles MIC with COLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is rich means it is absurd or ridiculous, hence comical.

clue.text: Take place successfully, though climax in poor taste

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plan or event comes off when it succeeds
second meaning: a crude phrase for reaching orgasm

explanation.walkthrough: 'in poor taste' marks the second sense as vulgar slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to succeed as planned and, crudely, to reach sexual climax.

clue.text: Bonked in the open air — given stiff treatment

parts.note: laid is slang for having had sex, as bonked is
out means outdoors

explanation.surface: Someone who had sex outdoors and was then treated harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' means a corpse: a body that is laid out is prepared for burial.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is called a stiff, and laying out is the preparation of a dead body for its funeral.

clue.text: Against being embraced by archdedcon transsexual

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words, as in an embrace

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Opposing a churchman who has changed sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being embraced by' shows the answer is held in 'archdedCON TRAnssexual'; 'archdedcon' is the source's misspelling of archdeacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Contra is Latin for opposite or opposing, used in English as a preposition.

clue.text: See 10
As may be seen by all, Neddy's turned a natural colour

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: a natural colour is one that has not been dyed

parts.words: As may be seen by all
parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

indicators.note: turned means the name's letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Neddy, a pet name for a donkey; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A donkey's coat has gone a natural shade.
explanation.walkthrough: A U-certificate film may be watched by anyone. 'turned' rearranges NEDDY to NDYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or fabric left in its original shade has not been tinted with any artificial pigment.

clue.text: Soul's destroyed wearing short skirt, according to leading fascist

indicators.note: the skirt is worn around the jumbled letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: destroyed means the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruined soul in a miniskirt, a would-be fascist pin-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to' is only a link. 'destroyed' turns Soul's into USSOL, which the skirt is 'wearing' around it, so the miniskirt image is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini founded Italian Fascism and led Italy as Il Duce.

clue.text: Go one better and expose party as gay?

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them as gay, the sense the end of the clue confirms
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A tabloid trying to beat rivals by outing a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as gay' fixes the sense of expose: to out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass them, doing better than they did.

clue.text: Roger Cobain roughly without interest

indicators.note: roughly means approximately, so the letters are only roughly as given and are rearranged
without means take out the interest letter

parts.note: i is the standard symbol for interest rate

explanation.surface: A rock star named Roger Cobain, bored stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Nirvana's singer was Kurt, not Roger, Cobain. 'without' removes I from COBAIN and 'roughly' rearranges COBAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Bacon was the thirteenth-century English friar and scientist, so his first name can clue his surname.

clue.text: Coincidence Cilla hosting Parkinson?

indicators.note: the words host the answer, holding it within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of coincidence and the start of Cilla

explanation.surface: Cilla Black presenting chat-show host Michael Parkinson, by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' shows the answer is held in 'coincidenCE CILla'. Parkinson here is Cecil Parkinson, the Tory minister, not the TV host.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil Parkinson was a Conservative cabinet minister under Thatcher, so his surname clues his first name.

clue.text: Players, etc, to transfer

indicators.note: transfer moves the letters into new positions

explanation.surface: Footballers and others being moved to another club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' sounds like footballers on a transfer, but they are musicians. ETCTO is reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight musicians performing together.

clue.text: Holy cigar! Surprisingly not many members control such a state

definitions.text: not many members control such a state

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at a cigar, followed by a remark on government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges the letters of HOLY CIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is a state ruled by a small group of people.

clue.text: Having no knockers to speak of, blooming well giving it all you' ve got

definitions.text: giving it all you' ve got

parts.words: Having no knockers to speak of
parts.note: flat-chested, knockers being slang for breasts
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: A flat-chested woman swearing as she tries her hardest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming well' reads as a mild British oath; 'well' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Going flat out means at full speed or with maximum effort.

clue.text: Dress was out in front, twisted

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
led means was in front, leading

explanation.surface: A dress that was leading the field got twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbled message is distorted or mixed up, twisted out of its true sense.
